reps.name: Andrew Alonso
reps.headlineGap: The recording ends mid-evaluation, so the entire decision and close half of the visit is unverified.
focus: Week 1: Record every call door to door and review one complete recording with a manager
Week 2: Ask the summer and winter thermostat question deliberately, always followed by the power-bill question
Week 3: Address membership status in the welcome before tools come out

reps.name: Andrew Trujillo
reps.headlineGap: Both recordings stop during the intake, so no findings, options or close were captured on either call.
focus: Week 1: Record every call door to door; review one complete recording with a manager
Week 2: Add the five-star seed, parking confirmation and floor protectors to the welcome
Week 3: Add the filter-frequency question to the intake block

reps.name: Benjamin Wyllie
reps.headlineGap: When customers ask what a replacement costs, he answers that pricing is a different department instead of proposing an appointment time.
focus: Week 1: Replace the repair-guy line with the sizing explanation and always propose a specific appointment time
Week 2: Ask the thermostat and power-bill questions before presenting any efficiency analysis
Week 3: Ask for the five-star review on every call, not just seed it

reps.name: Brandon Moreno
reps.headlineGap: A direct question about replacement cost was answered with a rough estimate instead of a booked specialist visit.
focus: Week 1: Run the three required questions as a fixed block at the thermostat on every call
Week 2: Add options, approval and today to the expectations block
Week 3: Convert every pricing question into a booked specialist appointment

reps.name: Cole Pantol
reps.headlineGap: Kept adding supporting arguments after the options were presented instead of stopping and letting the customer respond.
focus: Week 1: Present the options, deliver the closing line, then stay silent until the customer speaks
Week 2: Add filter frequency and the power-bill follow-up to the thermostat block
Week 3: Ask for the five-star review before leaving, not just seed it in the welcome

reps.name: David Canales
reps.headlineGap: The specialist visit was offered three times across two calls and never converted into a booked appointment.
focus: Week 1: Convert every price hesitation into a specialist appointment with a day and a time
Week 2: Run the three required questions as a fixed block at the thermostat
Week 3: Re-shoot unreadable photos before showing them, and ask for the review on every call

reps.name: Francisco Valencia
reps.headlineGap: None of the required assessment questions were asked on any call, so the customer's own bill and comfort evidence never entered the conversation.
focus: Week 1: Ask filter frequency, hot and cold rooms, and the thermostat and power-bill pair on every call
Week 2: Present one option line and one number at a time, pausing before the next
Week 3: Seed the five-star standard in the welcome and ask for the review before leaving

reps.name: Joe Mendoza
reps.headlineGap: Only one of the four required questions was asked across two calls, so both wins rested entirely on rapport and option-building.
focus: Week 1: Run all four required questions at the thermostat on every call
Week 2: Deliver the system teach-back instead of offering it and withdrawing it
Week 3: Ask for the five-star review before leaving every home

reps.name: Juan Tlatenchi
reps.headlineGap: The specialist visit was offered as something the customer might want rather than proposed with a specific day and time.
focus: Week 1: Ask filter frequency, hot and cold rooms, and the thermostat and power-bill pair on every call
Week 2: Propose a specific day and time for the specialist instead of asking whether they would like one
Week 3: Never leave a home without a repair date, a specialist appointment or an agreed callback time

reps.name: Mario Castro
reps.headlineGap: All three recordings end during the intake, so nothing after the questions was captured on any call.
focus: Week 1: Record every call door to door; review one complete recording with a manager
Week 2: Deliver the approval and today commitments in English, matching what is already said in Spanish
Week 3: Plant the five-star seed on every call in both languages

reps.name: Nathan Colquitt
reps.headlineGap: The expectations block covers only look and options, with no approval promise, today commitment or five-star standard.
focus: Week 1: Deliver all six expectation beats on every call
Week 2: Record every call door to door and review one complete recording with a manager
Week 3: Ask the summer and winter thermostat question deliberately on every call

reps.name: Nikko April
reps.headlineGap: A customer volunteered that he wanted replacement pricing and received general advice instead of a booked specialist visit.
focus: Week 1: Convert every replacement mention into a booked specialist appointment with a time
Week 2: Ask filter frequency and the power-bill question before asserting anything about energy costs
Week 3: Stop narrating uncertainty to customers; name the limit and promise the follow-up

reps.name: Robert Silinzy
reps.headlineGap: Five visits ended with information delivered and nothing scheduled, including one where the customer asked directly about replacement cost.
focus: Week 1: End every call with a repair date, a specialist appointment or a specific callback time
Week 2: Add the summer and winter thermostat question and the hot and cold rooms question to the intake
Week 3: Answer customer reasoning with a question rather than a correction
